title: Intake gate for precision slices & performance rollback policy
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: We currently accept low-precision model variants (INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ) into the model catalog with a binary pass/fail gate that focuses on token-level accuracy on a small canonical eval set. This has led to silent regressions in tail latency and SLO violations for a subset of customer workloads after rollout.

Goal: Introduce an intake gating mechanism that evaluates 'precision slices' (workload segments based on sequence length, prompt shape, and KV cache usage) and emits a deterministic fingerprint for each variant. Combine that with a staged canary rollout that includes an automated rollback policy when key SLO regressions or quality drifts are detected.

Acceptance criteria:
- New intake pipeline evaluates variants across at least 6 precision slices and records latency, p50/p95, and model output similarity metrics.
- Generated fingerprint stored alongside model artifact and surfaced in the console.
- Canary policy supports: (a) percentage-based traffic ramp, (b) automatic halt when p95 latency increases > 25ms or quality delta exceeds configured threshold, (c) automatic rollback to previous pin after two consecutive failing windows.
- Dashboard tile in Console with slice-level breakdown and boolean pass/fail per slice.
- Documentation and runbook for on-call response to canary failures.

Out of scope: quantization tooling to produce variants (this ticket assumes artifacts are provided by the quant pipeline), long-term drift detection (covered by ENG-51678).
acceptance_criteria: Slice-level metrics for at least 6 slices (latency/quality)
Fingerprint generated and stored with model artifact
Staged canary with automatic halt and rollback
comments: 2026-02-12 - Asha Menon: Kickoff meeting notes attached. Decided on initial 6 slices: short prompt (<64), medium (64-256), long (256-1024), chat-context (many turns), kv-heavy (large cache reuse), and streaming-heavy (frequent partial responses).

2026-02-18 - Diego Alvarez: Prototype intake harness implemented. It runs benchmark jobs in CI against provided variants and emits a CSV. Initial runs show INT8 GPTQ variant reduces cost but increases p95 by ~18ms on long sequences.

2026-02-25 - PM review (Lina Zhou): Concern raised about quality drift measurement. Agreed to add semantic-similarity (embedding cosine) and exact-match on handful of critical prompt families. Lina will provide 12 prompt families from customer telemetry.

2026-03-02 - Design sync (Ravi Patel): Dashboard mockups reviewed. We will show a traffic-split slider and a per-slice pass/fail badge. Design requests a machine-readable fingerprint format so the console can link to artifact diffs.

2026-03-05 - Diego Alvarez: Implemented canary controller with percentage ramp and stop/rollback hooks. Hook integrates with rollout service and emits events to the incident stream. Unit tests added for ramp policy and failure detection window.

2026-03-08 - QA (Sofia Kim): Ran end-to-end with toy model. Observed flaky failure detection on streaming-heavy slice due to noisy measurements. Added aggregation window (3 consecutive 5-minute windows) to reduce false positives.

2026-03-10 - Asha Menon: Trade-off decision: conservative rollback thresholds to prioritize reliability for enterprise customers. We will ship with default p95 delta threshold = +25ms and semantic-quality delta = -0.02 cosine. These can be tuned per-customer via Dedicated config.

2026-03-10 - Diego Alvarez: Linked PR is ready for merge pending infra review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/2146. Note: needs a release note and Console tile created in runtime-1.20 release.

Action items: (1) PM to produce prompt families (Lina) - done. (2) Infra to add rollout event permission (ENG-40227) - in progress. (3) Docs: create runbook and postmortem template for canary failures (Asha) - in progress.
